name: IWF/WOW WrestleFest '97

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline ("LIVE! From Skydome, Toronto, Canada, Sunday, March 16, 1997") and its Usenet posting date of 17 March 1997.

evidence.source: The federation's own broadcast script, subject "[IWF/WOW] WrestleFest '97 Part 1" through "Part 9" (17 March 1997)
evidence.note: Full announcer-narrated script for a supercard billed live from the SkyDome in Toronto; the sole and primary source for this record.

matches.note: Crusher pinned defending champion Johnny Rage with a small package to win the IWF National Championship.
"King" Kevin Payne retained the IWF United States Championship over Destroyer with a move billed as the Death Bomb.

eliminations.note: Eliminated together with "Diamond" Chris Carter as both men fell to the outside.

The broadcast's own count names Chris Carter eliminated twice, once alongside the Big Colossus and again minutes later by Joe Mills; both are recorded here as the source itself does not reconcile them.
Eliminated together with Power Warrior when a vertical suplex sent both men crashing to the floor.
Eliminated together with Len Griffen when a vertical suplex sent both men crashing to the floor.
Eliminated together with Christopher Stonebreaker late in the match.
Eliminated together with Iceman Krisp late in the match.
Eliminated together with Ric Rivas near the finish.
Eliminated together with Dan Watterson near the finish.

matches.note: A twenty-man non-title battle royal. Joe Mills outlasted the field; Curtis Conway is named among the entrants but the surviving script never states his own finish.
A non-title grudge match, billed on the broadcast as a rematch of Pyro's own original IWF World Title win over Unibomb; Unibomb won this time with a powerbomb.
Body Count ("Stunning" Anthony Thomas and "Vicious" Al Barber) retained the IWF/WOW World Tag Team Championship over America's Least Wanted (Joe Kidd and Octane).
The final of the IWF/WOW North American Tag Team Title tournament: Helter Skelter (Rex Rock and Casper) beat Horror (Dirt Dog and King Mort The Ruthless) to become the first champions.
matches.stipulation: IWF/WOW North American Tag Team Championship (tournament final)

matches.note: The Wrecking Crew (Jeff Waller and Jason Jarrett) and the Franchise beat the North American Alliance (Phil Clinton and Johnny Maple) and the Canadian Glacier; the Franchise pinned Maple, though Waller left hurt.
"Trouble Man" Martin Richards retained the IWF/WOW North American Championship over the Desert Scorpion when the referee counted both men out.
The Angel of Death, RedBack and Allen Shannon beat Johnny Skiles, Shawn Roberts and Vengeance; the Angel of Death pinned Roberts with a top-rope leg drop.
Jeremy "Roadkill" Thranton won the WOW World Heavyweight Championship from the Prophet, weeks after coming up short against Martin Richards for the North American title.
Derrick DaMann won the IWF World Heavyweight Championship from AJ "Black Ice" Stanson in the main event.

name: EGOS & ICONS: Day 1

matches.note: Two-ring War Games; Maverick, billed as champion Billy Rock's ally, was revealed as the opposing side's mystery partner and turned on Billy Rock, who submitted to his own finisher. Winning side received the last four entries into the Independence Day Rumble.
IC Title strap match; Maverick won the Intercontinental Championship.

A four-way #1 tag title contenders match (Ewiak Brothers, Infinite Justice, Intent to Injure, Down South Connection); the Ewiak Brothers were eliminated first, and Infinite Justice defeated the Down South Connection, though a co-president's decree later added the Down South Connection to the title match as well. Individual rosters for Infinite Justice and Intent to Injure are not fully named in the held text.
Ensassarol won by pinfall.
Result not stated in the held text.

notes: The first night of a two-night supercard.

name: EGOS & ICONS: Independence Day Rumble

matches.note: Thirty-man Independence Day Rumble for the vacant IWF/WOW World Heavyweight Championship; Razor Ron Jeremy outlasted twenty-eight others (including a mystery entrant) to become the new champion. Billy Rock, runner-up in a prior year's Rumble, announced his retirement afterward.
Liam Rogan and Gigantor won by submission.
Hightower won by submission (Canadian Classic Sharpshooter) and kept his place on the roster.

World Tag Team Championship; Infinite Justice (named here as Kenneth Morlock and Matt Allen per the prior night's action) defeated the Down South Connection to become new champions. The held text does not name the Down South Connection's own two wrestlers distinctly from Infinite Justice's; rostering is presumed from Day 1's own action.

notes: The second night of a two-night supercard, headlined by a thirty-man Rumble.

matches.note: Steve Greedy won the three-way.
Maverick won.
World Tag Team Championship; "Boys Next Door" (champions, only one member's action is described in the held text) lost the titles to Eric Travers and the Angel of Death.
McMannis won by disqualification.

appearances.source: IWF/WOW's own MAYHEM broadcast, 24 May 2002.

matches.note: Grudge match; Razor Ron Jeremy won.
North American Championship Casino Match; Kiljoy won the title from champion Jacen Canadi.
Hardcore Championship; Arcola won the vacant(-ly billed) title from McMannis.

World Heavyweight Championship vs Intercontinental Championship, best-of-five falls; Billy Rock won three falls to two (the deciding fall by submission, called by special guest referee Maverick), keeping the World title and winning the IC title as well.
